metaDescription: Six mushroom lamps compared on glass, ceramic, wood and silicone builds, bulb type, dimming, rechargeable power and size, with honest tradeoffs for nightstands.
expertTake: The ONEWISH translucent glass lamp is the best overall pick for its Murano-style hand-applied glass grains, standard E26 socket and 0 to 100 percent dimmer, while the Dawnwake 8.7 inch hand-blown lamp is the value pick for a small desk or shelf. The wood rechargeable touch lamp suits nurseries and cordless use. Anyone who needs real reading light, or who wants a lamp that stays cool and tough around toddlers, should skip glass mushroom lamps and choose silicone or a standard task lamp.
introParagraphs: A mushroom lamp is a small table lamp with a domed cap on a slim stem, a shape borrowed from mid-century design and Murano glass. It is more sculpture than lighting: the glow is soft and low, and the lamp earns its place on a nightstand, a shelf or a desk as a design object.

The materials range from hand-blown glass to ceramic, wood and silicone, and the practical differences are bulb type, dimming, power and durability. This guide compares six mushroom lamps on those points, and is honest that none of them is a reading lamp.

products.name: ONEWISH Vintage Translucent Glass Table Lamp, Black Glass Grain, E26 2700K Bulb, 0 to 100 Percent Dimmer

specList.label: Shade
specList.value: Translucent glass with hand-applied black glass grains

products.description:
ONEWISH makes a mushroom lamp with a translucent glass cap carrying hand-applied black glass grains, in a Murano vintage style, with an E26 socket, a 2700K LED bulb included and a rotary switch for dimming from 0 to 100 percent. The grains scatter the light so each lamp has its own play of shadow, and a 2700K bulb gives a soft warm glow.

An E26 socket is the standard household base, so you can change the bulb for any common type, which is not true of lamps that use tiny G9 bulbs. The tradeoff is fragility: glass can break if knocked, and a small lamp has a light base. Against the Dawnwake, the ONEWISH has a standard socket. Against the BOHON, it uses glass instead of ceramic.

Place the lamp at the back of the nightstand with the cord behind the table. Use a dimmable LED within the maximum wattage. Wipe the glass with a dry microfibre cloth, and avoid heavy pressure on the black grains. Check that the cap sits straight on the stem. Keep the lamp away from the table edge, and out of reach of toddlers and pets who might pull the cord.
products.bestFor: Bedsides and shelves that want a hand-finished glass mushroom with a standard bulb.
pros: Hand-applied black glass grains give a Murano-style play of light
A standard E26 socket takes any common bulb for easy replacement
A rotary dimmer covers 0 to 100 percent for bedtime and daytime
A 2700K bulb is included, so it works out of the box
cons: Glass can break if knocked, and a small base is easy to tip
It is a mood lamp and does not give enough light for reading

products.name: Dawnwake Orange Hand-Blown Glass Table Lamp, 8.7 Inch, G9 LED, Stepless Dimming
products.description:
Dawnwake's lamp is 8.7 inches tall, with a hand-blown glass mushroom shade in orange, a G9 LED bulb included and stepless dimming from a corded switch. A hand-blown technique means each shade is slightly different, with small variations in thickness and colour that give the lamp character.

At 8.7 inches it is compact enough for a shelf, a desk or a bedside table with little room, and the orange shade adds a warm accent. The tradeoff is the G9 bulb: it is a small bi-pin type that is harder to find than E26, so keep a spare. Against the ONEWISH, the Dawnwake is smaller and bolder in colour. Against the Glivpny, it has a hand-blown shade of a similar style.

Set the lamp on a flat, stable surface and dim it low in the evening. Use only the G9 bulb type and watch the maximum wattage. Wipe the glass with a dry cloth. Let the bulb cool before handling. The corded switch is easy to reach but can dangle, so tuck the cord behind the table.
products.bestFor: Desks, shelves and compact bedsides that want a small orange hand-blown accent.
pros: A hand-blown glass shade makes each lamp slightly unique
An 8.7 inch height suits shelves, desks and small tables
A G9 LED bulb is included and dims smoothly
A bold orange adds a warm mid-century accent
cons: A G9 bulb is harder to find than a standard E26 bulb
Glass can chip or break if the lamp is knocked over

products.name: Glivpny Orange Mid-Century Glass Table Lamp, Chrome Base, Hand-Blown, G9 Stepless Dimming

specList.label: Base
specList.value: Solid chrome with silver metal pole

products.description:
Glivpny pairs a hand-blown orange glass cap with a solid chrome base and a silver metal pole, a G9 LED bulb included and stepless dimming. A solid chrome base is weighty, which adds stability to a small lamp, and the silver finish gives a cool contrast to the warm orange glass.

The minimal design suits a modern or mid-century bedroom, and the dimmer lets you set a faint glow at night. The tradeoff is the G9 bulb and the usual glass fragility, and chrome shows fingerprints. Against the Dawnwake, the Glivpny has a heavier base and a metal pole. Against the ONEWISH, it uses a bulb type that is less common.

Wipe the chrome with a microfibre cloth to remove fingerprints, and the glass with a dry cloth. Use only the G9 bulb type, and keep a spare. Place the lamp at the back of the nightstand away from elbows. Dim to a low level in the evening. Check the pole screws after the first month, since a small lamp can loosen with handling.
products.bestFor: Modern bedrooms that want a weighted chrome base under a warm orange glass cap.
pros: A solid chrome base adds stability to a small lamp
A hand-blown orange glass cap gives a warm accent
Stepless dimming sets a faint night glow
A G9 LED bulb is included for immediate use
cons: Chrome shows fingerprints and needs regular wiping
G9 bulbs are harder to find than E26 bulbs

products.name: BOHON Ceramic Orange Bedside Table Lamp, Solid Wood Base, E12 2700K LED Included
products.description:
BOHON's lamp has a ceramic mushroom shade in orange, a solid wood base and an E12 candelabra bulb with a 2700K warm white LED included, in a retro aesthetic, and it is also sold in red. A ceramic shade is opaque and durable, so the lamp glows from the base of the cap rather than glowing through the shade as glass does.

Ceramic is less fragile than hand-blown glass, and a solid wood base adds weight. The tradeoff is the glow: an opaque shade gives a downward and outward wash of light, not a translucent glow, so the lamp looks different when lit. Against the glass lamps, it is tougher but less luminous. Against the wood rechargeable, it is a corded ceramic lamp.

E12 is a small candelabra base found in many hardware stores, so spares are easy to find. Place the lamp on a stable table and use a bulb within the maximum wattage. Wipe the ceramic with a barely damp cloth. Keep the wood base dry. Tighten the connection after a month.
products.bestFor: Bedrooms that want a tougher ceramic mushroom with a wood base.
pros: A ceramic shade is tougher than hand-blown glass
A solid wood base adds weight and a warm material contrast
An E12 bulb is easy to find and a 2700K LED is included
A retro orange is also offered in red
cons: An opaque shade gives less luminous glow than glass
A small candelabra bulb limits brightness

products.name: Beech Wood Rechargeable Touch Night Light, Small Bedside Mushroom Lamp for Nursery and Bedroom

specList.label: Control
specList.value: Touch, long press to adjust brightness

products.description:
This small bedside lamp is made of beech wood, runs on a rechargeable battery with no cord and uses touch control, with a long press to adjust the brightness from the brightest down. A wooden shell is warm to the touch and does not shatter, which suits a nursery or a child's room better than glass.

A cordless lamp can be placed anywhere, carried to the bathroom at night and moved between rooms, and the soft light is a better fit for a night light than for a task lamp. The tradeoff is runtime and brightness: the data we reviewed does not state battery hours, and small rechargeable lamps need charging every few days. Against the silicone lamp, it is firmer and more decorative. Against the glass lamps, it is tougher and cordless.

Charge the lamp fully before first use, and set a regular day to recharge it. Use a low brightness for a night light to extend runtime. Wipe the wood with a dry cloth, and avoid water. Keep the charging cable out of reach of small children. Place it where it will not be knocked into water, since the battery is sealed.
products.bestFor: Nurseries and bedrooms that want a cordless, tough, soft night light.
pros: Beech wood is warm to the touch and does not shatter
A rechargeable battery means no cord and flexible placement
Touch control with long-press dimming is easy in the dark
A soft light suits a night light
cons: Battery hours are not stated in the data we reviewed
A small rechargeable lamp needs charging every few days

products.name: Rechargeable Soft Night Light, BPA-Free, Tap and Remote, Multi-Colour LED, Dimmable

specList.label: Control
specList.value: Hand tap and remote within 35 ft

products.description:
This soft silicone night light is made from BPA-free silicone described as non-toxic, rechargeable and cordless, controlled by a hand tap or a remote that works within 35 feet, with multi-colour dimmable light. Silicone is soft and bounces, so the lamp survives being dropped by a child and is gentle to hold, which suits a nursery, a toddler's room or a night feed.

The soft warm light is meant to comfort children in the dark, and the remote lets you change settings without lifting the baby. The tradeoff is that it is a night light, not a lamp: the output is low, multi-colour modes are a novelty and the data we reviewed does not state battery hours. Against the wood lamp, it is softer and more child-safe but less decorative. Against the glass lamps, it is tough and cordless.

Charge the lamp fully before first use, and recharge it when it dims. Use a warm white or low-brightness setting at night, since bright colours can be stimulating. Wipe the silicone with a damp cloth. Keep the charging cable out of reach of small children. Check the seams for wear if a child chews on it, and retire it if the silicone is damaged.
products.bestFor: Nurseries and toddlers' rooms that want a soft, drop-proof, cordless night light.
pros: Soft BPA-free silicone survives drops and is gentle to hold
A rechargeable battery means no cord near a child
A remote within 35 feet and a hand tap give easy control
Dimmable multi-colour light suits a night feed or bedtime routine
cons: Output is low, so it is a night light and not a lamp
Battery hours are not stated in the data we reviewed

buyingCriteria.explanation: Hand-blown glass, as on the ONEWISH, Dawnwake and Glivpny, glows beautifully but breaks. Ceramic, as on the BOHON, is tougher. Wood and silicone, as on the cordless lamps, survive knocks and suit children's rooms. Choose by who will be near the lamp.

E26, as on the ONEWISH, is the standard household base. E12, as on the BOHON, is a small candelabra base found in most shops. G9, as on the Dawnwake and Glivpny, is a small bi-pin bulb that is harder to find. Keep a spare of whichever type your lamp uses.

A rotary or stepless dimmer, as on the ONEWISH and Dawnwake, lets you drop the glow low for bedtime. Mushroom lamps give mood light, so a reading lamp is a separate purchase. Check the bulb lumens against your needs.
A corded lamp runs all night but needs an outlet. A rechargeable lamp, like the wood and silicone ones, moves anywhere but needs charging every few days and its battery hours are rarely stated.
Mushroom lamps are small, from about 8.7 inches tall upward. A small lamp has a light base and is easy to knock over, so place it at the back of a surface and away from edges.

Orange and red glass are bold mid-century accents. Black grain glass reads as Murano vintage. Wood and silicone read as nursery and Scandinavian. Match the lamp to the room's palette under warm bulbs.

howToChoose.subheading: Glass vs Ceramic vs Wood and Silicone

cards.label: Glass (ONEWISH, Dawnwake, Glivpny)
cards.text: Luminous and decorative, but fragile and often with less common bulbs.

cards.label: Ceramic, wood, silicone (BOHON, cordless lamps)
cards.text: Tougher and safer around children, but less luminous or less decorative.

howToChoose.note: Choose glass for a nightstand design piece, and ceramic, wood or silicone for children's rooms.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A cordless, drop-proof body, a warm low light and a control you can reach without lifting a child.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The silicone lamp has a remote and a soft body, and the wood lamp has touch control.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want a hand-finished glass design piece with a standard bulb, as with the ONEWISH.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You only need a soft night light; the silicone or wood lamp is enough.

maintenance.why: Dust dulls glass and chrome. A dry microfibre cloth is safe.
G9 and E12 bulbs are small and sometimes out of stock. A spare avoids a dark lamp.
Small batteries run down. A regular charging day keeps the lamp ready.
Small lamps are easy to knock over. A damaged cord should be replaced.
Small bulbs get hot in a closed cap. Wait before touching.

faq.q: Can I read by a mushroom lamp?
faq.a: Not well. They give soft mood light. Use a focused reading lamp for books.
A small bi-pin bulb base used in compact lamps. It is less common than E26, so keep a spare.

faq.q: Are glass mushroom lamps safe for children's rooms?
faq.a: They can break, so silicone or wood is safer. Keep glass lamps out of reach.

faq.q: How long does a rechargeable lamp last?
faq.a: It depends on brightness and battery size, and many listings do not state hours. Recharge every few days.

faq.q: Can I change the bulb colour?
faq.a: Yes, on lamps with standard sockets. Warm 2700K is the usual choice for a bedside.

faq.q: How do I clean a mushroom lamp?
faq.a: Unplug it and wipe with a dry cloth. Avoid water on wood and electronics.
